Q: Unpacking a list / tuple of pairs into two lists / tuples A: 
>>> source_list = [('1','a'),('2','b'),('3','c'),('4','d')]
>>> list1, list2 = zip(*source_list)
>>> list1
('1', '2', '3', '4')
>>> list2
('a', 'b', 'c', 'd')

Warning: This will fail if the list is empty!

Edit: Note that zip(*iterable) is its own inverse:

>>> list(source_list) == zip(*zip(*source_list))
True

When unpacking into two lists, this becomes:

>>> list1, list2 = zip(*source_list)
>>> list(source_list) == zip(list1, list2)
True

Addition suggested by rocksportrocker.

Q: How to remove line breaks from a file in Java? A:

tl;dr

myString.lines().collect( Collectors.joining( "" ) )

Details

You asked two different questions:

  • How to remove line terminators from a string
  • How to remove line terminators from a file

String

The first is incompletely answered by AbstractVoid. Let’s complete that now.

The method String#lines returns a Stream of String objects, one per line within your source string. The following line terminators will have been removed by that method:

  • A line feed character "\n" (U+000A).
  • A carriage return character "\r" (U+000D).
  • A carriage return followed immediately by a line feed "\r\n" (U+000D U+000A).

A stream’s CharSequence (interface of String) elements can be joined together. The result is a single string, just what you desire.

You neglected to mention if you want a new delimiter or not. If not, pass empty string ("").

String joined = myString.lines().collect( Collectors.joining( "" ) )

For example the hard-coded string "a\nb\nc\n" result is “abc”.

File

For your other question, removing line terminators from lines of a file, the solution is quite similar. Use Files.lines to get a Stream of the lines read from the file, and then join.

The stream from the file must be used in try-with-resources syntax to ensure the stream, and its underlying open file, are closed.

Q: PHP date() format when inserting into datetime in MySQL A:

The problem is that you're using 'M' and 'D', which are a textual representations, MySQL is expecting a numeric representation of the format 2010-02-06 19:30:13

Try: date('Y-m-d H:i:s') which uses the numeric equivalents.

Q: Get SQL to create the table equivalent of an existing view A:

This isn't fully bullet-proof (I'm not escaping column names that are reserved keywords, for example), but reading from information_schema.columns and splicing together a CREATE TABLE statement worked for me:

SELECT format(E'CREATE TABLE %s (\n    %s\n);\n', table_name,
string_agg(format('%s %s %s', column_name, data_type,
  CASE WHEN (is_nullable = 'YES') THEN 'NULL' else 'NOT NULL' END),
  E',\n    ' order by ordinal_position))
FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'other_schema'
AND table_name = 'my_table' GROUP BY table_name;

Q: Sheets Found in Workbook But Code Stops Running A:

I made a small change to the testing of the sheet existence. The sheet names are in an array, and if any of it is missing a message is thrown. If you want to use your original method, then change Or to And, or use Not for every result. That will checks all worksheet names not any.

    If Not (SheetExists("NL21") And SheetExists("US12")) Then

or use

    If Not SheetExists("NL21") Or Not SheetExists("US12") Then

The second For...Each loop calls a function, which will execute the formula checking on all sheets and return a result of the test.

Sub formulacheck()

Dim item, formularesult
arr1 = Array("NL20", "NL21", "US12")

For Each item In arr
    On Error Resume Next
    If Not Worksheets(item).Type = xlWorksheet Then
        MsgBox "One sheet is missing", vbCritical
        Exit Sub
    End If
Next item
On Error GoTo 0

For Each item In arr
    formularesult = formulafunction(item)
    'do something with formularesult
    MsgBox "The worksheet " & item & ": " & formularesult, vbInformation
Next item

End Sub

Function formulafunction(sheet As Variant) As Variant

Dim ws As Worksheet, wb As Workbook
Set wb = ActiveWorkbook
Set ws = wb.Worksheets(sheet)
'checking formula the returned formulafunction can be anything e.g. True or False or text "Succeed"/"Failed"
result = "Succeed"
formulafunction = result

End Function

Q: How to create a 'feed' for users (DB Design)? A:

I think it will be easier if you indeed create an extra table with the user's activity. Checking all those tables, from which you probably don't even need all data, and then format those to a feed is going to take a toll on your server. Also think on the future (eg. what if you were to have 100's of these tables).

Using an extra table allows you to just query the feed-table and use this info. Without having to extract this from the correct tables, as the data in the tables aren't probably useful directly and needs some calculations.

Another point you may consider is future changes to the feed. Say you want to display some more info on the feed, but the appropriate tables don't have that info, you would have to change all these tables (not to mention the scripts/pages that use them to also add the info). But with one feed-table you can add one more element and change the feed-creation method.

Q: git undo all uncommitted or unsaved changes A:

I just stumbled upon a GitHub repository that made undoing something in Git very easy. It’s called ugit.

Just type ugit, and it provides to you a list of options that you can choose to undo that Git command.
